newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar eases as truck supplies flowing again.
newsitem.headline: India sugar eases as truck supplies flowing again.

text.p: Indian sugar prices continued falling as supplies from mills arrived in greater quantities in the aftermath of a nationwide truck strike, traders said.
Sluggish consumer buying and increased supplies weighed on prices lower while stockists remained active sellers.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 25/40 rupees to 1,290/1,325 rupees per quintal while M-30 fell by 10/25 rupees to 1,350/1,415 rupees per quintal.
"Arrivals of sugar from the mills to the market improved following conclusion of the truckers strike," one broker said.
"We are witnessing daily arrivals of about 80/100 truck loads in the Bombay market," he said.
One truckload carries 9/10 tonnes of sugar.

Meanwhile, sugar mill delivery prices bounced back on the back of increased lifting of sugar from mills by traders and a reduction in mills overstocked positions. Sugar mill delivery rose by 5/10 rupees to 1,220/1,240 rupees per quintal.

Trading in the mill delivery, however, remained slow as most of the delivery tenders for the free sale quota for first half of current month are exhausted. Trading volume for mill delivery will improve again after commencement of the second half.
